source_documents.title: Monosulfonicpillar[5]arene: Synthesis, Characterization, and Complexation with Tetraphenylethene for Aggregation-Induced Emission

reference_evidence_units.quote: the crosspeak A indicates that H4 is in close contact with Hd, He
reference_evidence_units.subject: G1 and MSP5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Model guest G1 in chloroform, NOESY and titration.
reference_evidence_units.statement: G1 shows intermolecular NOESY contacts and a reported association constant of (1.08 +/- 0.22) x 10^2 per molar.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: G1 is a small model guest, not TPE-(Br)4. Do not transfer its association constant or full binding pose to the target.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The proton NMR spectrum of MSP5 with TPE-(Br)4 in d-chloroform solution was also obtained and similar complexation-induced chemical shift changes were detected
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-(Br)4 with MSP5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Target-host mixture in deuterated chloroform; main text reports SI Fig. S58.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Target-specific chemical shift changes are reported as consistent with host-guest complexation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The underlying SI spectrum is not in this packet; the main-text report is retained without claiming an independent rereading of the spectrum.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Strong emission in dilute solution was observed from the complex of TPE-(Br)4⊂MSP5
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-(Br)4 with MSP5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Fig. 3b spectra at 2 micromolar in chloroform; photographs at 200 micromolar, 298 K.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The combined host-guest sample emits strongly while separate components are essentially nonemissive at the same concentration.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Spectra and photographs use different concentrations. This observation alone does not identify the nonradiative pathway.

reference_evidence_units.quote: formation of host-guest inclusion complex that restricts the intramolecular rotation of phenyl rings
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-(Br)4 with MSP5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Host titration and increased target fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors explain the enhancement through host-assisted restriction of phenyl rotation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No direct torsion dynamics measurement is shown; this source interpretation is supported indirectly by binding and control experiments.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the fluorescence of TPE-(Br)4 was almost unchanged
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-(Br)4 with DMP5 or MCP5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Alternative hosts in chloroform, Fig. 4a and main-text control description.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Alternative host binding does not reproduce the MSP5 turn-on. The source explicitly argues binding alone is insufficient.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This is a negative control on a generic binding-sufficiency claim, not evidence against all host-guest effects.

reference_evidence_units.quote: No fluorescence was observed when M1 mixed with TPE-(Br)4
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-(Br)4 with noncyclic sulfonic fragment M1
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Fig. 4b, sulfonic-group control without the pillar cavity.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The sulfonic fragment alone does not produce the turn-on seen with MSP5.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The joint host structure and assembly context matter; neither a cavity alone nor an isolated sulfonic group explains all controls.

reference_evidence_units.quote: self-assemble into nanoparticles with the average diameter of 16 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-(Br)4 with MSP5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Main text summarizes SEM, DLS, Tyndall effect and DOSY; underlying Fig. S60-S61 are not supplied.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source reports a common diffusion behavior and nanoparticle formation around 16 nm for the combined sample.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Reported assembly evidence, not a resolved packing structure or proof of excitonic/excimer emission; SI data not independently inspected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The solubility of the host-guest complex (fluorescent nanoparticles) in chloroform was reduced due to the hydrophilic group
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-(Br)4 with MSP5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Assembly in chloroform; interpretation integrating alternative hosts and sulfonic-group controls.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source couples host-assisted restriction of motion with reduced solubility and aggregation in explaining emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Confinement and RIM describe overlapping aspects of the same pathway, not necessarily separate additive mechanisms.

reference_evidence_units.quote: intensity decreased gradually upon raising the temperature
reference_evidence_units.subject: TPE-(Br)4 with MSP5
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Temperature cycle, Fig. 5c-d; 1 micromolar in THF.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Emission decreases on heating and recovers on returning to room temperature.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Temperature experiments use THF rather than the chloroform binding titrations; intensity alone cannot distinguish disassembly from increased nonradiative motion.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Retain the source's host-assisted RIR explanation, explicitly as an indirect mechanistic interpretation rather than measured rotation dynamics.

reference_mechanisms.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Nanoparticle formation and altered solubility provide the external assembly context for motion restriction. This overlaps with host binding and RIM.

reference_mechanisms.label: HOST_GUEST_INTERACTION
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Target complexation and appropriate host architecture are central to the turn-on. Negative controls exclude a blanket claim that any host binding is sufficient.

mechanism_decisions.label: ICT_TICT_CT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No target-specific charge-transfer assignment or diagnostic comparison is established in the selected evidence.

mechanism_decisions.label: ESIPT_PT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No excited-state proton-transfer mechanism is established. Changing solution pH or ground-state protonation alone does not establish ESIPT.

mechanism_decisions.label: PET_ET
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No photoinduced electron-transfer pathway is established by the selected source evidence.

mechanism_decisions.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Particle formation and AIE alone do not establish H/J excitonic or excimer emission; no such target assignment is established here.

mechanism_decisions.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Lifetime or intensity changes alone do not isolate radiative rates or a distinct bright/dark-state mechanism. Do not duplicate a generic nonradiative explanation as a separate established pathway.

mechanism_decisions.label: TRIPLET_METAL_ENERGY_TRANSFER
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No target-specific triplet, metal-mediated or energy-transfer mechanism is established in the selected evidence.

mechanism_decisions.label: RACI_CI_ACCESS
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No target-specific conical-intersection calculation or assignment is established in the selected evidence.

mechanism_decisions.label: SOKR_ANTI_KASHA
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No higher-state emissive mechanism or anti-Kasha assignment is established in the selected evidence.
